1	# The agent follows the app's own Koda, and Prelude installs it only with the person's approval
2	status: proposed
3	date: 2026-10-23
4	parts: designs, pages, installs, server, agent, host, branches
5	
6	## Context
7	Every prompt points the agent at Prelude's own installed Koda (`server/main.js` resolves `@kodalang/core`), so an app on another version gets guidance for attributes it doesn't have. Upgrading an app's Koda needs `npm install`, which the agent can't run and nothing in Prelude does. `node_modules` isn't in git, so a fresh worktree has none, and merging an upgrade leaves the old Koda installed in the person's checkout.
8	
9	## Decision
10	`designs` finds the app's Koda and reads its version from `node_modules/@kodalang/core/package.json`: first in the worktree (the app's path from `prelude.json`, then the root), then the same in the project's own checkout, and Prelude's only when neither has one. It also reads the version the app's `package.json` asks for. The server passes the Koda it found to every prompt as `kodaPath` and to `--add-dir`, and the design host serves its runtime to a design's pages (`/_prelude/koda/`), so designs behave as the app will; Prelude's own pages keep Prelude's.
11	
12	`pages` compares the app's version with Prelude's on the project page and offers an upgrade, which starts a fix. A new part, `installs`, runs the project's package manager (chosen by its lockfile) in two places: in that fix's worktree, installing Prelude's version, and in the person's checkout once the upgrade is merged, installing the version `package.json` asks for. `pages` offers that second install when the checkout's installed Koda isn't the one it asks for. Either way the command is fixed (never one the agent wrote), names only `@kodalang/core`, has a time limit, and runs only after the person approves it, seeing it first, as with a host: install scripts are code from outside the project.

The architecture is right here. The code just hasn't been written yet, so this is the planned gap, not drift. I'd keep the decision and build the code.

**Why the check reports it**
- `prelude/prelude-architecture/architecture/parts/installs.md:5` lists `files: server/installs.js` as the part's file. That file doesn't exist; nothing under `server/` matches `*install*`.
- The part comes from decision D-k7v (`architecture/decisions/D-k7v.md`), which is still `status: proposed`. It was written on 2026-10-23 as the target, the same way `server/words.js` was. The notes say so: `prelude/prelude-architecture/NOTES.md:15` reads "Until it's built, the check reports `server/installs.js` missing."
- None of D-k7v is built yet, not just this file. `server/main.js:49` still finds Prelude's own Koda (`import.meta.resolve('@kodalang/core')`) and passes that same `kodaPackage` to every prompt (`main.js:1897`, `2008`, `2025`, `2162–2168`). `designs` doesn't look for the app's Koda in the worktree or checkout yet, and `pages` has nothing that offers an upgrade.

**Why not change the architecture instead**
Dropping `installs` would undo choices you made on 2026-10-23 (`NOTES.md:16–18`): the install runs only with your approval, it only ever installs `@kodalang/core`, and the one place Prelude changes your checkout is limited to `node_modules`. The point of putting this in its own part is to keep that fence in a single file. Nothing has happened since then that argues against it.

**What I'd change, on a branch**
- **New `server/installs.js`:** picks npm, pnpm or yarn from the app folder's lockfile. It builds the fixed command `install @kodalang/core@<version>` itself, with nothing taken from the agent. It runs only in a worktree `branches` made or in the project's own folder, only after you've seen and approved the command, with a time limit. It keeps the output for the chat. It only depends on `branches` and `designs`, as `installs.md:6` says.
- **`server/designs.js`:** finds the app's Koda (worktree, then checkout, then Prelude's) and its installed and requested versions.
- **`server/main.js`:** passes the Koda that `designs` finds as `kodaPath` instead of `kodaDir`. Adds the "Upgrade Koda" route that starts a fix and the approve-install step, and serves the app's runtime at `/_prelude/koda/`.
- **Pages:** the project page offers the upgrade, and after the merge offers the install in your checkout (`flows/koda-upgrade.md`, steps 2 and 12).
- **Once it's built:** mark D-k7v accepted and remove the "until it's built" line in `NOTES.md:15`.

Adding only an empty `installs.js` would quiet the check, but nothing would call it. It's better to build it as part of the koda-upgrade flow.

1	# Prelude architecture
2	
3	Prelude is a tool for designing and then building an app with an agent: you pick a project, chat with the Claude Code CLI, and watch the design appear beside the chat. It runs as one Node server (plain `node:http`, views in Eta, Koda in the page) on localhost:4200, optionally inside a Tauri desktop window. Everything it produces is files in the project's `prelude/` folder, each design worked on in its own git branch and worktree. Agent-written views render in a sandboxed child process, and each design is served on its own preview origin.
4	
5	## Layers
6	
7	1. Windows
8	2. Entry points
9	3. Pages
10	4. Agent and live state
11	5. Designs and hosting
12	6. Project files
13	7. Shared helpers
14	8. Outside
15	
16	## Principles
17	
18	- **The folder is the database.** Everything Prelude makes is a file under the project's `prelude/`, committed with the code; `~/.prelude/` holds only machine-local conveniences, so nothing is lost if it's deleted.
19	- **The server is the single source of truth for live state.** Every window (chat, pop-out, browser tab) renders from the server and re-renders on its SSE events, so no window holds state another needs.
20	- **Agent-written code never runs in the server's process.** A design's views render in a sandboxed renderer, and a host that runs them unsandboxed starts only once the person approves it.
21	- **The agent works with ordinary file tools, fenced to what it may touch.** It reads the project and the folders added as references, writes only where its mode allows, and deletes by writing a file empty.
22	- **A design's memory is its files, not a conversation.** Each session starts from NOTES.md, the views and states, so sessions on different machines and branches pick up where the work stands.
23	- **Committed files must merge cleanly.** Session folders and decision ids are random, transcripts are append-only, and there's no shared index that every session rewrites.

I added `server/installs.js`, so the architecture check should stop reporting it missing. Nothing calls it yet, so you won't see any change in Prelude. I couldn't run anything, so the new tests haven't been run.

**What the new file does**
- **Package manager:** it uses npm, pnpm or yarn, depending on which lockfile the app has (the app's folder first, then the project root).
- **Command:** it builds the command itself, and it only ever installs `@kodalang/core` at an exact version. It refuses ranges like `^0.2.0`, tags like `latest`, and anything with extra words in it, so nothing the agent writes can change what gets installed.
- **Where it runs:** only in your project's own folder or in a worktree Prelude made for it. It finds the app inside that folder from `prelude.json`'s app path.
- **Approval:** `plan()` gives back the command for you to see, and nothing runs until `approve()`. `decline()` drops it.
- **Time limit and output:** an install is stopped after 5 minutes, and its output is kept for the chat.
- **Worktree vs checkout:** in a fix's worktree it saves the exact version, so the fix commits `package.json` and the lockfile. In your checkout, npm runs with `--no-save`, so only `node_modules` changes.

It only uses `designs` (the app path) and `branches` (which worktrees exist), as the Installs part allows. Nothing else in the code, designs or architecture changed; I just updated the "until it's built" line in `prelude/prelude-architecture/NOTES.md`. The fix's notes are in `prelude/fixes/server-installs-js-in-installs-doesn-t-match-the/NOTES.md`.

**Tests:** I added `test/installs.test.js`. Run `node --test test/installs.test.js`, then `npm test`.

**Two things for you to decide**
1. pnpm and yarn have no "don't save" option. In your checkout they rewrite `package.json` and the lockfile with the version the merge already put there, which should leave the same content. Is that fine, or should installs in your checkout be npm-only?
2. The rest of the Koda upgrade (decision D-k7v) still isn't built:

   - The project page has no "Upgrade Koda" or "install it here" offer.

text:
I've built the rest of the Koda upgrade, including small changes to the project page. I couldn't run the tests or the server, so none of this has been run yet. Prelude's check after this turn will show whether the pages render and the architecture matches.

**What you'll see on the project page**
When the app is built and uses Koda, the app card now shows one of these at a time:
- **Upgrade Koda**, when the app's version is older than Prelude's. The card shows the command first, and clicking the button is your approval, install scripts included, the same way Run works. It starts a fix called "Upgrade Koda to <version>" on its own branch and opens that fix's page.
- **A link to that branch** while the upgrade fix is in progress.
- **Install Koda <version>**, once the upgrade is merged and your folder still has the old version (`node_modules` isn't in git). Only `node_modules` changes.
- **Installing…** while an install runs, or the last of its output if it failed.

Each button only does what the card is offering at that moment, so a form can't ask for a different version or package.

**What I changed in the code**
- **Prompts and the design host:** every agent prompt now gets the app's own Koda: the branch's copy first, then your folder's, and Prelude's only if neither has one. The design host serves that same Koda to designs.
- **The upgrade fix:** Prelude installs the new version on the branch and writes the fix's notes. When the install finishes it commits `package.json` and the lockfile, unless the agent is mid-turn, in which case that turn's commit picks them up. You then tell the agent in the fix to update the views for the new version.
- **The Project Landing Page design:** its typical state now shows the "Upgrade Koda" offer, it has the two new form posts, and its notes have a section explaining why.
- **No architecture change needed:** the Installs, Designs, Server, Page models and Design host parts already describe all of this, so I didn't propose any decision. I only updated the architecture notes to say it's built.

**Tests:** run `node --test test/installs.test.js`, then `npm test`.

**Things to check**
- The typical state's approved screen will now differ on the app card. That's on purpose.
- Try it end to end on a project with an older Koda: click Upgrade Koda, confirm the fix opens, and confirm its branch gets `package.json` and the lockfile committed once the install finishes.
- pnpm and yarn can't install without saving. In your folder they rewrite `package.json` and the lockfile with the version the merge already put there, which should change nothing.
- The design host serves the folder holding the app's Koda entry file, and pages load `koda.js` from it. An older Koda whose entry file isn't named `koda.js` wouldn't load.
- Installs are kept in memory. If Prelude restarts, a failed install's output is lost and the card simply offers it again.

The fix's notes are in `prelude/fixes/server-installs-js-in-installs-doesn-t-match-the/NOTES.md`.
